text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm rolling an experimental routing policy that prefers nearest zone by ping, but falls back to cheapest region if latency > 120ms. Wanted to flag a few UX/headers questions before I flip it on for canary tenants.
kevin: Nice. What does the API look like for forcing/opt-out? We need a clear escape hatch for some enterprise customers.
maya: Right now there's an internal header: X-RW-Proximity-Mode: prefer|force|off. prefer lets policy run, force pins to nearest even if cost spike, off disables proximity steering.
olga: Hmm, enterprise legal asked we never silently change region for data-residency customers. How do we ensure force/off interacts with tenant config? Should tenant config trump headers?
jamal: tenant config should always win. Headers are request-scoped and can be used by proxies, but not to override a tenant's residency constraint. That's how Dedicated/Private works today.
kevin: Agree. So precedence: tenant residency whitelist > tenant routing policy > request header. Make sure that's documented in console and API.
maya: Good. Also debating whether to add a query param ?prefer_nearby=1 for SDKs — easier for quick tests but messy for proxies that might strip query params.
olga: I'd avoid query param as canonical. If SDKs need a dev-mode toggle, expose a client config flag. Keep network-level control via headers.
jamal: Operational concern: when we fall back to cheaper region, we need telemetry tags for cost-and-latency correlation. Proposal: add routing.tags = ["proxied_nearby", "fallback_cost_region:eu-west-2"] and emit to traces/metrics.
sre-bot: Deploy checklist: ensure new tag emitted to trace sampling (1p95), add metric rw.routing.proximity.fallback.count, and a debug log at DEBUG level with route decision and {latency_ms, cost_delta_pct}.
maya: I'm also adding a soft-sla guard: if fallback cost delta > 40% AND request has enterprise_org tag, refuse fallback and route local with a cost-warning metric.
kevin: UX in Console: for canary tenants show a new card on route decisions with a small timeline and reason (e.g., "latency 142ms > 120ms -> cost fallback eu-west-2"). Need to add a compact explanation for support.
olga: Regarding header precedence, suggestion: X-RW-Region-Hint for advisory (low trust), X-RW-Region-Override for force. Override only accepted if tenant allows header-overrides. That should satisfy compliance.
jamal: One more: how do we handle KV cache affinity? If we bounce regions for same session keys, cache misses will spike. We should include a sticky_token header or route cookie TTL >= 30s when using prefer to avoid churn.
maya: Good catch. Will add Set-Cookie: rw_route_sticky=zone:us-west-2; Max-Age=30 when prefer selected. But we need to opt-out for private deployments.
kevin: Can we get a small config snippet for the runtime team? e.g.:
```
routing_policy:
  mode: proximity
  latency_threshold_ms: 120
  cost_delta_limit_pct: 40
  header_precedence: [tenant_config, X-RW-Region-Override, X-RW-Region-Hint]
  sticky_ttl_s: 30
```
Use that in the rollout PR.
maya: Perfect — I'll open the rollout PR and include tests for: tenant-residency, header overrides allowed/disallowed, telemetry tags, sticky cookie behavior. Planning canary to 5% of production in us to start.
deploy-bot: maya scheduled canary rollout: routing/proximity v2 -> 5% @ 2026-04-02T15:00Z :rocket:
kevin: Thanks — let's also add an annotation to the canary dashboard that explains cost tradeoff and a quick link to revert policy to 'off'. :+1:
